title: Multi-column DROP (a, b) — the column-list form of a column drop
expected_feedback: Critical: `ALTER TABLE … DROP (col, col)` is Oracle's column-list form and does exactly what `DROP COLUMN` does, twice — it destroys both columns' data, auto-commits, and cannot be crossed by FLASHBACK TABLE. It carries no smaller risk for being written more compactly, and a review that only recognises the `DROP COLUMN` spelling will wave it straight through. No copy of ORDERS is taken here, so both columns are unrecoverable the moment this runs. Snapshot them first, keyed: CREATE TABLE mig_bak_orders_... AS SELECT id, legacy_a, legacy_b FROM orders. Classify the phase restore/PITR.
violated_rule: Irreversible statements need a pre-DDL artefact
